subject.title: [Feature]: Feature Request: Batch Tool Calls + Context Block Management + Plan Enforcement

question: Should OpenClaw pursue any of these native core surfaces now: file/search batching, AI-callable context blocks, or runner-enforced submitted plans?
rationale: The request changes core tool schemas, session/context persistence semantics, and enforcement/config policy, while repository vision only partially aligns and warns against heavy orchestration or optional capability in core without a clear API gap.

options.title: Split for design review
options.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella and ask maintainers to sponsor narrower design tracks for any surface they want to pursue.

options.title: Route extensible pieces outside core
options.body: Defer core changes unless a plugin/API gap is proven, using current context-engine, tool plugin, and external workflow seams where adequate.

options.title: Close as out of scope
options.body: Decide that native batching, context-block tools, and plan-enforcement orchestration are not planned for core at this time.

recommendation.title: Split for design review
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella and ask maintainers to sponsor narrower design tracks for any surface they want to pursue.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest adjacent history on update_plan and strict-agentic behavior, which makes him the best available owner for the product-direction choice.
